content: 1. A study conducted by Wingood et al. (2013) examined racial differences and factors associated with the potential adoption of pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) for HIV prevention. The findings were based on a national survey and published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes. 2. Another study by Wingood et al. (2013) explored participant motivations for enrolling and continuing in the FEM-PrEP HIV prevention clinical trial. This research was presented at the 7th IAS Conference on HIV Pathogenesis and Treatment. 3. Research by et al. (2013) investigated the acceptability of PrEP among men who have sex with men (MSM) and transgender women in Northern Thailand. The results were published in PLoS ONE. 4. A 2014 study by et al. focused on the interest in PrEP among female sex workers in Guangxi, China. The findings were published in PLoS ONE. 5. A study titled Troubling Innovation (2013) explored the acceptability of antiretrovirals for HIV prevention among vulnerable communities. This research was published in the International Journal of STD and AIDS. 6. Research conducted in 2014 examined barriers to the uptake and use of PrEP among communities most affected by HIV in the UK. The findings were based on a qualitative study in Scotland and published in BMJ Open. 7. A 2013 study investigated awareness and willingness to use PrEP among gay and bisexual men in Scotland, with implications for biomedical HIV prevention. The results were published in PLoS ONE. 8. Research by et al. (2013) assessed attitudes toward PrEP among MSM in Western China. The findings were published in AIDS Patient Care and STDs. 9. A 2012 study explored factors associated with willingness to use oral PrEP among MSM in Shenyang, China. The findings were presented at the 19th International AIDS Conference. 10. A study conducted in 2011 examined the acceptability of PrEP among female sex workers in Xinjiang, China. The findings were published in the Journal of Zhejiang University (Medical Sciences). 11. Research in 2012 investigated attitudes toward PrEP among drug users from high-risk populations for AIDS in Western China. The findings were published in the Academic Journal of the Second Military Medical University. 12. A 2012 study assessed the willingness to accept PrEP among Chinese MSM. The findings were published in PLoS ONE. 13. Matthews et al. (2012) reviewed the use of antiretrovirals for safer conception among HIV-serodiscordant couples. The findings were published in Current Opinion in HIV and AIDS. 14. Young et al. (2014) reviewed the acceptability of antiretrovirals for preventing sexually transmitted HIV, focusing on oral PrEP and treatment as prevention. The findings were published in AIDS and Behavior. 15. A systematic review and meta-analysis conducted in 2015 examined the use of oral PrEP for individuals at substantial risk of HIV infection. 16. Kennedy et al. (2014) reviewed the values and preferences of MSM and transgender individuals regarding PrEP, based on existing literature. 17. Kennedy et al. (2012) reviewed the values and preferences of serodiscordant couples regarding PrEP, based on existing literature. 18. Kennedy et al. (2012) reviewed the values and preferences of MSM and transgender individuals regarding PrEP, based on existing literature. 19. Schneiders (2014) conducted a qualitative study on the values and preferences of transgender individuals regarding PrEP. 20. Henderson (2014) summarized the values and preferences of key populations regarding HIV prevention, harm reduction, and related issues. 21. Henderson (2014) consolidated a report on the values and preferences of key populations regarding HIV prevention and harm reduction. 22. Henderson (2014) explored the values and preferences of people who inject drugs, as well as the views of experts, activists, and service providers on HIV prevention and harm reduction. 23. A consultation by INPUD and UNAIDS in 2014 focused on PrEP for people who inject drugs, with a meeting report from Chisinau. 24. UNAIDS, WHO, and Wits (2013) discussed the hopes and fears of sex workers regarding PrEP, providing recommendations from a discussion meeting. 25. A global consultation in 2014 examined the experiences and perspectives of sex worker communities regarding PrEP and early treatment as HIV prevention strategies. 26. The Global Forum on MSM and HIV (2014) conducted a qualitative study on the values and preferences of MSM regarding the use of antiretroviral therapy as prevention.
